description: Check whether management delivers what it promises: past guidance and commitments against results, leadership changes and insider trades. Alpha on credibility.
suggested_questions: Check management's track record at Boeing (BA) since Kelly Ortberg became CEO in August 2024.
Check management's track record at Starbucks (SBUX) since Brian Niccol became CEO in September 2024.
Check management's track record at Peloton Interactive (PTON) since Peter Stern became CEO in January 2025.
skill:
Where management's record lives:
- Commitments and guidance: earnings releases (8-K exhibit 99.1), prepared remarks and slides on the IR site, investor
  day presentations, shareholder letters, conference webcasts summarised by the company. Reported results in later
  releases and 10-Q/10-K filings are the outcome.
- Leadership changes: 8-K Item 5.02 (departures, appointments, interim roles), the leadership page now and in
  archived copies at web.archive.org, press releases.
- Insider trades: Form 4 filings on EDGAR (open-market purchases code P, sales code S, footnotes naming a 10b5-1 plan,
  option exercises code M); Form 144 notices of proposed sales.
- Pay and incentives: the DEF 14A compensation discussion, which shows the metrics management is paid on.
- Background: prior companies' filings and press on how those tenures ended.

What terms mean:
- A commitment is a dated, specific, checkable statement: a target, a date, a launch, a cost saving, a margin level.
  Vision statements are not commitments.
- Outcomes: met, exceeded, missed, partially_met, withdrawn (quietly dropped or no longer mentioned), pending (date
  not reached), cannot_verify.
- Sandbagging: beating by a similar margin every period, which suggests guidance set low on purpose. Overpromising:
  repeated misses or targets withdrawn without explanation.
- Open-market insider purchases carry more signal than sales; planned 10b5-1 sales carry little on their own.
- New CEOs lean on forward-looking promises before they have a record; a commitment made in the first year is worth
  checking hardest.

Where the alpha is: the gap between what management said and what it did is visible across several old releases
side by side, and few readers line them up.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: Management track record for one listed company.

commitments.description: Dated, checkable commitments and what happened, oldest first.

items.description: Dated, checkable commitments and what happened, oldest first.

commitment.description: The commitment, quoted or closely paraphrased.

target_date.description: When it was due, YYYY-MM-DD or period.

outcome_evidence.description: What later results or statements show.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

outcome_source_url.description: Full URL of the page showing the outcome.

guidance_history.description: Guidance per period: first given, last updated, actual.

items.description: Guidance per period: first given, last updated, actual.

latest_guidance.description: Last update before the period ended.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.
